findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined for this bucket, so objects (including the vendor-roster.xlsx seed object) are stored unencrypted at rest by default, risking exposure of sensitive report data.

findings.issue_category: no bucket ACL / public access block
findings.description: No acl is set and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, leaving it dependent on AWS defaults with no explicit guard against accidental public exposure via later ACL or policy changes.
The bucket stores ledger export data (likely financial/sensitive) but has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving data unencrypted at rest.
The bucket has versioning and logging configured but no server_side_encryption_configuration, so stored model artifacts are unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined for this bucket, so operational runbook content is stored unencrypted at rest.

The acl value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid canned ACL and appears to be a typo of 'log-delivery-write'. If it resolves to that grant, it gives the S3 log delivery group write access to an audit trail bucket, which should be tightly scoped; as written, the invalid value is also a misconfiguration that could fail apply or behave unpredictably, undermining the integrity guarantees expected of an audit log bucket.

force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be deleted without recourse, and combined with the absence of versioning this increases the risk of irreversible loss or destruction of report data, including by an attacker seeking to destroy evidence.
